RGDP.name: Gross domestic product
RGDP.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted chain volume gross domestic product.

RHFCE.name: Household consumption
RHFCE.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted chain volume household final consumption expenditure.

RDI.name: Dwelling investment
RDI.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted chain volume dwelling investment.

RBI.name: Business investment
RBI.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted chain volume business investment.

RPD.name: Public demand
RPD.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted chain volume public demand.

RGNE.name: Gross national expenditure
RGNE.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted chain volume gross national expenditure. Gross national expenditure is domestic final demand plus the change in the level of inventories.

RMTPGDP.name: Major trading partner (export-weighted) GDP
RMTPGDP.definition: Year-ended growth of export weighted seasonally adjusted volume index of gross domestic product of Australia’s major trading partners.

Imp.name: Imports
Imp.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted chain volume imports.

Exp.name: Exports
Exp.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted chain volume exports.

ToT.name: Terms of trade
ToT.definition: Year-ended growth in the relative, seasonally adjusted, prices of exports to imports.

Emp.name: Employment
Emp.definition: Year-ended growth of quarter-average of seasonally adjusted monthly employment level.

UR.name: Unemployment rate (quarterly, %)
UR.definition: Quarter-average of seasonally adjusted monthly unemployment rate.

HUR.name: Hours-based underutilisation rate (quarterly, %)
HUR.definition: Middle month of quarter. Seasonally adjusted by the RBA.

NWPI.name: Wage Price Index
NWPI.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted Wage Price Index excluding bonuses and commissions.

NAENA.name: Nominal average earnings per hour (non-farm)
NAENA.definition: Year-ended growth of the ratio of seasonally adjusted non-farm compensation of employees to seasonally adjusted non-farm total employee hours.

RHDI.name: Real household disposable income
RHDI.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted household disposable income, deflated using the household final consumption expenditure deflator. Household disposable income is gross household income less income payable.

CPI.name: Consumer Price Index
CPI.definition: Year-ended growth of non seasonally adjusted all groups Consumer Price Index.

TMI.name: Trimmed mean inflation
TMI.definition: Year-ended growth of trimmed mean inflation. Trimmed mean inflation in each quarter is computed using seasonally adjusted inflation of each expenditure class in that quarter.

CR.name: Cash rate (%)
CR.definition: Target ‘cash rate’,  which is the interest rate on unsecured overnight loans between banks. The RBA has made different assumptions about the cash rate in different SMP rounds. From May 2024 SMP onwards, the cash rate is assumed to move broadly in line with expectations derived from financial market pricing.

TWI.name: Trade-weighted index (index)
TWI.definition: Trade-weighted index (TWI) of the Australian dollar. The daily TWI is assumed to be unchanged at its current level going forward.

Crude.name: Brent crude oil price (US$/bbl)
Crude.definition: Brent crude oil price quoted in US$/bbl. Prior to May 2026 SMP, it was assumed to remain constant at the current price over the current quarter. For the rest of the forecast period oil prices were expected to remain around the price implied by the six-month-forward rate. From May 2026 SMP, current quarter oil prices are based on observed spot prices to date and market pricing for the remainder of the quarter. For the rest of the forecast period, brent crude oil prices are guided by market pricing.

ERP.name: Estimated resident population
ERP.definition: Year-ended growth of non seasonally adjusted estimated resident population. The population assumption is underpinned by  a range of sources, including partial indicators from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, migration policies, and estimates made by the Australian Government.

GDPpHW.name: Labour productivity
GDPpHW.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted chain volume non-farm gross domestic product per hour worked.

HSR.name: Household savings rate (%)
HSR.definition: Household savings rate refers to the ratio of household saving (disposable income minus consumption) to household disposable income, net of depreciation.

RWPI.name: Real Wage Price Index
RWPI.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted Wage Price Index excluding bonuses and commissions deflated by seasonally adjusted all groups Consumer Price Index.

RAENA.name: Real average earnings per hour (non-farm)
RAENA.definition: Year-ended growth of seasonally adjusted average earnings per hour deflated by seasonally adjusted all groups Consumer Price Index.

GDPPC.name: GDP per capita
GDPPC.definition: Derived from GDP and resident population growth: 100 × [(1 + GDP/100)/(1 + population/100) − 1].

models.name: MARTIN · public 2019
models.description: Local linearisation of all 217 equations in the RBA’s public 2019 workfile, around its saved baseline. Some public source series are simulated. Ordinary shocks are one-quarter equation innovations; the cash rate then follows the model rule.

mappingNotes.GDPpHW: GDP per total hour response applied to the non-farm productivity forecast.
mappingNotes.HSR: Model saving ratio applied to the RBA household savings ratio; accounting definitions may differ.
mappingNotes.TWI: Nominal TWI response; baseline index multiplied by the percentage change.
mappingNotes.Crude: World oil-price response; baseline oil price multiplied by the percentage change.
mappingNotes.RHDI: Model household disposable income deflated by consumption prices.
mappingNotes.NAENA: Model average earnings response applied to non-farm average earnings.
mappingNotes.GDPPC: Derived from GDP and population growth. MARTIN’s working-age population response proxies total population; age composition is held fixed.

models.name: DINGO · 2026 released baseline
models.description: Baseline solution released with Fink & Hambur (2026), extending the Gibbs–Hambur–Nodari model with separate mining-investment dynamics and updated parameter estimates. Uses baseline price rigidity, not the paper’s alternative rigidity scenarios or the current internal RBA model. The cash rate responds endogenously after impact.

mappingNotes.TMI: Quarterly model inflation is estimated using trimmed-mean CPI (RDP 2018-04, section 3.2 and Appendix A); four quarterly responses are summed for year-ended inflation.
mappingNotes.RBI: Non-housing sector investment, weighted by published model steady-state investment shares.
mappingNotes.RMTPGDP: The model foreign-output response is applied to the RBA trading-partner aggregate.
mappingNotes.TWI: Cumulative nominal appreciation; baseline index multiplied by the percentage change.
mappingNotes.ToT: Export-value minus export-volume response, less import-value minus import-volume response.
mappingNotes.GDPPC: Derived from GDP growth, holding population on the RBA baseline path. DINGO has no population shock response here.
